title: Storeroom: typed, versioned repair snippet repository + policy-aware executor
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Problem: On-call engineers and SREs often re-create ad-hoc repair scripts in Slack or personal snippets. This leads to inconsistent remediation outcomes, lack of provenance, and security exposure when privileged commands are executed manually. Storeroom is a centralized, typed snippet repository plus an execution service that enforces policy, RBAC, and safe dry-run semantics to make small remediations reproducible, auditable, and reviewable.
acceptance_criteria: API and web UI to create, view, and version typed snippets (schema, inputs, safe-defaults)
Execution service supports dry-run, plan-preview, and audited live run modes with single-click approval for P0/P1 snippets
RBAC gates enforced: only allowed roles can run live; others can request run via canary or require approval
WASM-based sandboxed execution path for untrusted snippets; privileged adapters for cluster-only approved snippets
Integration with runbooks-as-tasks: snippets can be embedded as atomic steps and surfaced in incident playbooks
Telemetry: per-run token and route-level cost/latency metadata, plus success/failure metrics and post-run diagnostics linked to the snippet version
E2E tests and a staging dashboard demonstrating rollback and replayability
implementation_notes: Catalog model: Git-backed index for human editability + DB index for fast lookup. Each snippet is a SHA-versioned artifact with YAML metadata (inputs/types/policies)
Execution isolation: evaluate using tiny WASM runtime for-most; provide an operator-only adapter (k8s job) for network-privileged actions with mandatory approval flow
Policy enforcement: use existing RBAC service; add snippet-level allowlists and mutable policy tags (canary, requires-approval, emergency-only)
Dry-run semantics: run in simulator mode (replay logs + side-effect mocking) and produce a plan diff shown in UI/CLI
Audit trail: immutable run records stored in long-term storage with linkable run IDs surfaced in Console traces
Backward compatibility: export/import hooks for existing ad-hoc admin scripts; migration tool to convert common scripts into typed snippets
Safety-first UX: disable live-run by default for new snippets; require badge/approval to certify for live execution
Telemetry hooks: emit snippet.id, snippet.version, requester.role, route, latency_ms, tokens_used, result.status to observability pipeline
